t: You're on Gracechurch Street, a main road running through the City of London, the historic and financial centre of the capital. It's the birthplace of Peter Collinson, the English botanist. He was a keen gardener and a Fellow of the Royal Society. In Georgian London he acted as a middleman for an international exchange of scientific ideas, passing knowledge between people in different places. It's a busy commercial street now, and it's a good reminder that the City has produced thinkers as well as bankers.
